body.x: Solvit System (CEO Yeong-Goo Kim) won a CES 2026 Innovation Award with its “intelligent radio relay drone operation system,” which rapidly detects people in distress even in radio shadow zones.

Following last year’s Innovation Award for “iSAR,” an intelligent search support system that dramatically narrows search areas in radio shadow zones, Solvit System earned recognition for two consecutive years by unveiling “SOLVIT-BRIDGE,” a technology that uses radio waves to find actual missing persons faster and more reliably.

Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News and also a judge for the CES 2024 and CES 2026 Innovation Awards, met with Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System, to discuss the significance of the consecutive awards, core technologies, on-site responses, and global expansion strategies.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please share your thoughts on winning the Innovation Award.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: Last year, we received an Innovation Award for iSAR, our intelligent search support system, and this year, we are honored to win again with our intelligent radio relay drone operation system. We developed this technology through a public innovation R&D project by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and we could complete it thanks to support from rescue organizations such as the Gyeongnam Provincial Police Agency and the Gangwon Fire Academy, as well as public data provided by the Korea Communications Agency. I sincerely thank everyone who collaborated with us.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Please introduce the technology that won the Innovation Award.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: We won the Innovation Award in the Smart Communities category with SOLVIT-BRIDGE. As the name suggests, it means building a bridge of life for people stranded in radio shadow zones.

The iSAR system we won with last year narrowed the search area for missing persons by about 25 to 1. SOLVIT-BRIDGE takes the next step by conducting faster, more reliable searches within the narrowed area.

Currently, rescue sites use video drones, but limited visibility and obstacles such as vegetation or rocks make detection difficult. Radio relay drones transmit radio beams and check device responses, so they do not suffer from terrain limitations. As long as the device is not completely powered off, detection is possible even if the person cannot answer calls or has lost consciousness.

This approach allows searches about 200 times faster than human searches and 10 to 50 times faster than video drones, which is the greatest advantage because rescuers can locate people before their phone batteries run out.

body.x: Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: How has the on-site response been?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: iSAR already sees active use by the Gyeonggi Northern Fire Services, the Gangwon Fire Headquarters, and the Korea Mountain Rescue Association, and feedback from the field has been very positive.

We successfully completed demand-side field demonstrations for SOLVIT-BRIDGE at the end of last year, and we plan to supply it after registering it as an innovative product. Supply is expected via the Gyeongnam Provincial Police Agency as early as the end of this year, or at the latest by next spring.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: Do you provide the entire drone-mounted service, or can other companies operate it by mounting only the required equipment?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: We are not a drone manufacturer. The core of the radio relay drone lies in the search relay device and the software that intelligently operates the drone; Solvit System supplies both components. We design the system so that drones from any manufacturer can integrate with it and operate as third-party devices.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: I understand you also operate in the defense sector.

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: About 95 percent of our business comes from the defense sector. We applied radio analysis technologies used in defense to public life-saving applications. Although we do not yet have public-sector revenue, we plan to expand into that area. Overseas demand for such technologies is strong, so we target markets such as the United States, Australia, Canada, and Brazil, where radio shadow zones are common, and territories are large.
Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News (left), and Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System (right), pose after the CES 2026 Innovation Company interview | Photo by AVING News
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What core know-how made the Innovation Award possible?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: First, the search area narrowing technology of iSAR developed last year must connect with the SOLVIT-BRIDGE technology. These two technologies need to work together to create cooperation, as SOLVIT-BRIDGE alone has limited effectiveness.

Second, the key lies in the intelligent operation of the radio relay drone. The system defines the search area, prioritizes zones with a higher probability of locating a missing person, and adjusts beam width and output based on terrain shielding and signal attenuation.

Third, the system incorporates a patent-pending technology that detects whether a device exists within the beam, even if the person has collapsed and cannot respond, without requiring any response from the phone itself.
Q. Joseph Choe, Editor-in-Chief of AVING News: What are your future plans?

A. Yeong-Goo Kim, CEO of Solvit System: This technology closely relates to mobile communications and emergency rescue, so we have already confirmed participation in MWC next March. We will also participate in FDIC, the largest firefighting exhibition in the United States, in May, and we have reserved a booth for INTERSCHUTZ, the world’s largest firefighting exhibition held in Hannover, Germany, in June. It will be our first time exhibiting there, and we have high expectations.
These exhibitions offer opportunities to introduce our technology directly to end users and to find local partners for supply and collaboration.
